661	- Ein Vorlagenpaket und kapitelweise Generierung aus dem Prozess-/Story-Arbeitsstand. Eine Unternehmenswissensbasis ist keine Voraussetzung.
662	- Browserbearbeitung, Autosave, Revisionen und Vorschlagsvergleich.
663	- Regelprüfung und ergänzender KI-Review.
664	- Manuelle strukturierte kaufmännische Angaben.
665	- Word-Entwurf und finale Word-Fassung aus festen Revisionen.
666	- Dauerhafte Aufträge, Fehlerbehandlung und betriebliche Diagnose.
667	
668	### Etappe 2: Fachliche Erweiterung
669	
670	- Weitere geprüfte Vorlagen und Projektprofile.
671	- Erweiterte Rollen-, Prozessvarianten- und Map-Sichten nach konkretem Bedarf.
672	- Optionale Unternehmenswissensanbindung und verbesserte Suche bei nachgewiesenem Nutzen.
673	- Schätzvorschläge, Kalkulationsbausteine und bestehende Freigaberegeln.
674	- Wiederverwendbare Referenzen, Optionen und Varianten mit klarer Gültigkeit.
675	
676	### Etappe 3: Integration und Zusammenarbeit
677	
678	- Postfach-, Meeting-, SharePoint- oder CRM-Anbindungen nach konkretem Bedarf.
679	- Gleichzeitige Zusammenarbeit, wenn der Pilot einen ausreichenden Nutzen zeigt.
680	- Word-Vorschau, strukturierter Word-Reimport oder Rückführung freigegebener Bausteine als jeweils eigener Umfang.
681	
682	Konkrete Zeit- und Aufwandsangaben folgen nach Prüfung der vorhandenen Vorlage, der Zielumgebung und repräsentativer Eingaben. Ein universeller Import beliebiger Dokumentlayouts oder ein autonomer Angebotsversand sind keine Voraussetzung für den beschriebenen Nutzen.
683	
684	## 18. Qualitätsprüfungen der Angebotswerkstatt
685	
686	Die folgenden Prüffälle betreffen die Umsetzung dieser Angebotswerkstatt. Sie werden **nicht** an die erzeugten User Stories angehängt. Das Zielangebot enthält weiterhin einfache Stories ohne Akzeptanzkriterien.
687	
688	| ID | Prüffall | Erwartetes Ergebnis |
689	|---|---|---|
690	| A01 | E-Mail, Audio, Konzept und PPTX einem Angebot hinzufügen | Jede Quelle besitzt einen Status und erreichbare Herkunft; Probleme einzelner Quellen bleiben sichtbar |
691	| A02 | PDF enthält eine Scan-Seite, Folie eine relevante Grafik | OCR beziehungsweise visuelle Auswertung wird genutzt oder die Lücke ausdrücklich ausgewiesen |
692	| A03 | Zwei Quellen widersprechen sich zu Scope oder Termin | Konflikt mit beiden Fundstellen; keine unbemerkte Auflösung durch das Modell |
693	| A04 | Quellen nennen weder Preis noch garantierte Zielgüte | Entwurf enthält keine erfundene verbindliche Preis- oder Erfolgszusage |
694	| A05 | KI entwickelt einen neuen Lösungsansatz | Inhalt wird als Vorschlag geführt und nicht als bereits belegte Unternehmensleistung ausgegeben |
695	| A06 | Nutzer bearbeitet ein Kapitel und lädt die Seite neu | Gespeicherter Inhalt einschließlich erlaubter Tabellen und Listen bleibt erhalten |
696	| A07 | Ein Modellaufruf endet nach einer manuellen Änderung | Ergebnis erscheint nur als vergleichbarer Vorschlag; manuelle Änderung bleibt unverändert |
697	| A08 | Zwei Bearbeiter speichern auf derselben Ausgangsrevision | Zweiter widersprüchlicher Speichervorgang erzeugt einen sichtbaren Konflikt |
698	| A09 | Ein bestätigter Aufwand oder Scope wird verändert | Verknüpfte Kapitel und Bestätigungen werden als erneut zu prüfen markiert |
699	| A10 | Nutzer hat keinen Zugriff auf ein fremdes Angebot | API, Suche, Quellenzugriff und Export liefern keine fremden Inhalte |
700	| A11 | Finaler Export enthält Pflichtlücken oder blockierende Konflikte | Finale Ausgabe wird mit verständlichen Gründen verhindert; Entwurf bleibt möglich |
701	| A12 | Export nach abgeschlossener Bearbeitung | DOCX enthält die gewählte Revision, korrekte Kapitel und editierbare Inhalte in der vorhandenen Vorlage |
702	| A13 | Modell- oder Exportdienst schlägt fehl | Gespeicherte Arbeit bleibt erhalten; Status und gezielter neuer Versuch sind verfügbar |
703	| A14 | Neue Vorlagenversion wird veröffentlicht | Bestehende Angebote behalten ihre gebundene Version bis zur bewussten Migration |
704	| A15 | Text wird nach einer positiven Quellenprüfung umgeschrieben | Bisherige Belegzuordnung wird nicht als unverändert gültige Prüfung ausgegeben |
705	| A16 | Word-Entwurf wird heruntergeladen und extern geändert | Anwendung behauptet keine automatische Synchronisation dieser Änderungen |
706	| A17 | Nutzer übernimmt einen KI-Text mit einer neuen Scope-Entscheidung | Neue Textrevision entsteht; fachliche Entscheidung bleibt bis zur ausdrücklichen Bestätigung offen |
707	| A18 | Freier Text widerspricht dem bestätigten Aufwand oder Scope | Befund und ausdrücklicher Abgleich; finale Ausgabe bleibt bis zur Auflösung gesperrt |
708	| A19 | Ein neues Angebot erhält ausreichend beschriebene Kundenquellen | Erstes fachliches Arbeitsergebnis ist eine User Story Map der Kundenprozesse mit verknüpften einfachen Stories |
709	| A20 | Stories werden initial erzeugt oder neu formuliert | Je Story einfacher Satz aus Rolle, Ziel und Nutzen; keine Akzeptanzkriterien, Given/When/Then-Blöcke oder angehängten Prüflisten |
710	| A21 | Keine Unternehmenswissensbasis ist vorhanden | Map, Stories, Lösungsvorschläge und Kapitel können trotzdem aus Kundeneingaben und Nutzerentscheidungen entstehen |
711	| A22 | Kundenprozess enthält Rückfragen, Übergaben oder Varianten | Zusammenhänge werden verständlich erfasst oder als offen markiert; es wird keine durchgängig lineare Reihenfolge erfunden |
712	| A23 | Nutzer ordnet Stories neu oder verschiebt sie in eine Option | IDs bleiben stabil; angebotener Scope, Map und abhängige Kapitel werden nachvollziehbar abgeglichen |
713	| A24 | Word wird erzeugt | Fachlicher Inhalt beginnt mit einer lesbaren editierbaren Map und einfachen Stories; sie verwenden denselben Revisionsstand wie die Kapitel |
714	| A25 | KI schlägt zusätzliche Stories oder einen Skeleton vor | Vorschlagsherkunft bleibt sichtbar; neue Stories erweitern den angebotenen Umfang nicht automatisch |
715	| A26 | Quelldokument beschreibt nur technischen Bedarf oder lässt Prozessschritte offen | Offene Fragen oder nachvollziehbare Prozessvorschläge; keine erfundenen Kundenentscheidungen |
716	| A27 | Nutzer ändert eine Story nach manueller Kapitelbearbeitung | Map und Story werden versioniert; betroffene Kapitel werden markiert, manuelle Texte nicht stillschweigend überschrieben |
717	
718	Zusätzlich wird jedes Vorlagenpaket anhand von Referenzdokumenten strukturell und visuell geprüft. Eine erfolgreiche Dateierzeugung allein erfüllt die Word-Abnahme nicht.
719	
720	## 19. Erfolgsmessung und Betrieb
721	
722	### 19.1 Vorgeschlagene Pilotziele
723	
724	Die folgenden Werte sind **zu validierende Zielhypothesen**, keine gemessenen Leistungsversprechen. Für den Pilot werden mindestens zehn repräsentative Angebotsfälle gegen den bisherigen Arbeitsablauf verglichen.
725	
726	| Kennzahl | Messung | Vorgeschlagenes Ziel |
727	|---|---|---|
728	| Aktive Bearbeitungszeit | Zeit bis zum fachlich akzeptablen Entwurf gegenüber vergleichbaren bisherigen Fällen | Median mindestens 30 Prozent geringer |
729	| Nachbearbeitungsaufwand | Fachreview klassifiziert strukturellen und inhaltlichen Änderungsbedarf | Mindestens 70 Prozent der Kapitel benötigen höchstens begrenzte Überarbeitung |
730	| Prozessverständnis | Fachreview vergleicht Map und Stories mit den im Testfall bekannten Kundenzielen und wesentlichen Aufgaben | Kein wesentlicher beschriebener Prozessschritt im akzeptierten Stand unbemerkt ausgelassen; zusätzliche Schritte als Vorschläge erkennbar |
731	| Einfachheit der Stories | Prüfung von initialen und überarbeiteten Stories | Einfache Rolle-Ziel-Nutzen-Sätze ohne automatisch ergänzte Akzeptanzkriterien |
732	| Kritische unbelegte Zusagen | Fachreview von Preis, Termin, Leistungsumfang und Erfolgsversprechen | Keine unmarkierte unbelegte kritische Zusage im final akzeptierten Stand |
733	| Inhaltsgleichheit beim Export | Automatischer Strukturvergleich und visuelle Prüfung der Referenzfälle | Kein verlorener oder unbemerkt veränderter unterstützter Inhaltsblock |
734	| Schutz manueller Änderungen | Revisions- und Konflikttests | Kein stilles Überschreiben in den definierten Konfliktfällen |
735	| Kosten und Laufzeit | Je Phase und Angebot; Audioverarbeitung separat | Im Pilot erfassen und anschließend belastbare Budgets vereinbaren |
736	
737	Der Pilot definiert vorab, was „begrenzte Überarbeitung“ bedeutet. Zehn Fälle dienen der ersten Entscheidung und sind kein statistischer Nachweis allgemeiner Qualität. Eine Win-Rate lässt sich daraus nicht seriös ableiten.
738	
739	### 19.2 Kosten- und Laufzeittreiber
740	
741	- Länge und Qualität der Audiodateien.
742	- OCR und visuelle Auswertung im Vergleich zu nativen Dokumenten.
743	- Umfang der Kundenquellen, Zahl der Prozessvarianten, Stories und Überarbeitungsschleifen.
744	- Zusätzliche Such- und Wissensaufrufe nur dann, wenn sie tatsächlich verwendet werden.
745	- Anzahl und Größe gemeinsam generierter Kapitel.
746	- Zusätzliche Review- und Verbesserungsschleifen.
747	
748	Extraktion und gegebenenfalls Indexierung werden bei unveränderten Quellen wiederverwendet. Gezielte Prozess-, Story- und Kapitelvorschläge ersetzen unnötige Vollgenerierung. Pro Auftrag gelten ein Aufrufbudget, Fristen und Abbruchregeln. Modellkosten sind getrennt von optionalen Such-, Speicher-, Betriebs- und gegebenenfalls Editorlizenzkosten zu betrachten.
749	
750	## 20. Vor der Umsetzung zu konkretisieren
751	
752	| Entscheidung | Verantwortungsbereich | Bedeutung |
753	|---|---|---|
754	| Konkrete Word-Vorlage, Map am Beginn des fachlichen Inhalts, Pflichtkapitel und geschützte Texte | Fachverantwortliche und Vorlagenverantwortliche | Bestimmt Kapitelmodell und Exportnachweis; Stories bleiben ohne Akzeptanzkriterien |
755	| Zielumgebung, Identität und zulässige Modellverarbeitung | Architektur und IT-Betrieb | Bestimmt Adapter, Zugriffe und Betriebsform |
756	| Welche ergänzenden Unternehmensinhalte wiederverwendbar sind, falls gewünscht | Wissens- und Angebotsverantwortliche | Bestimmt optionale Wissensbestände; blockiert nicht den Start ohne Wissensbasis |
757	| Wer kaufmännische Felder bestätigen darf | Angebots- und Vertriebsverantwortliche | Bestimmt Rechte und Abschlussregeln |
758	| Behandlung von Audio, Aufbewahrung und Löschung | Produktverantwortliche mit zuständigen internen Stellen | Bestimmt Importprozess und Lebenszyklus |
759	| Unterstützte Vorlagenfunktionen und Editor-/Word-Parität | Entwicklung mit Vorlagenverantwortlichen | Bestimmt den nachweisbaren Funktionsumfang |
760	
761	Diese Entscheidungen verhindern nicht die Verwendung dieses Dokuments als fachliches Zielbild. Sie werden vor den jeweils abhängigen Umsetzungsschritten konkretisiert.
762	
763	## 21. Quellen und Einordnung
764	
765	### Ausgangsanalyse
766	
767	- Fachliche Präzisierung vom 23. Oktober 2026: Kundenanforderungen und umzusetzende Prozesse als Mittelpunkt; User Story Map als Startartefakt; einfache Stories ohne Akzeptanzkriterien; Unternehmenswissen optional.
768	- [Alloq: Story Map](/Users/Jens.Rehpoehler/Workspace/Projekte/alloq/docs/features/story-map.md:66): Aktivitäten, Aufgaben, Stories, Slices und Walking Skeleton als Strukturvorbild. Historische Releasezuordnungen werden nicht in eine Angebotsplanung übernommen.
769	- [Alloq: Story-Format](/Users/Jens.Rehpoehler/Workspace/Projekte/alloq/docs/guide/contributing.md:246): Stabile IDs und Rolle-Ziel-Nutzen-Satz als Vorbild. Die dort beschriebenen Akzeptanzkriterien und Code-/Testnachweise sind ausdrücklich kein Bestandteil der hier erzeugten Angebotsstories.

# Refined prompt: "Angebote" page as new package `alloq-offer`

> Load `alloq-implementation` first, then `appkit-mantine-reference` before using any `mn.*` component you have not used in this task. Follow the test-first workflow and definition of done from that skill.

## Task

Add a new page **Angebote** (`/offers`) that lists offers calculated for customer projects. It looks and behaves like the Projekte list view: a macOS-style table with status groups, a toolbar with search, filter segments and a "Angebot anlegen" button, and an inspector on the right that shows the clicked offer. Offers can be created and edited, but never deleted; they can be archived and restored.

The feature lives in a **new, independent uv workspace package `components/alloq-offer`** (import name `alloq_offer`). Entity, model, repository, services, states, components and the page factory all live in this package. It depends only on `alloq-commons` and appkit, never on `alloq-project`, `alloq-team`, `alloq-dashboard` or `app`.

Access is controlled by a **new permission role `offer_editor`** (label "Angebote"). Admins, project managers and users with `offer_editor` may see and edit offers. Nobody else sees the page or its sidebar entry.

## Context (found in the repo)

- Reference slice to copy the shape from: the Projekte list view.
  - Page factory: `components/alloq-project/src/alloq_project/pages.py` → `create_projects_overview_page` (uses `app_page`, `window_toolbar`, `viewer_only(..., fallback=no_access())`).
  - Table: `alloq_project/components/project_table.py` (`TEMPLATE`, `COLUMNS`, `_row`, `_group`, `split_view`, `list_header`, `list_row`, `cell_main`, `badge`, `number`, `empty_list`).
  - Inspector: `alloq_project/components/project_inspector.py` (`inspector`, `inspector_section`, `key_values`, `plain_button`, inline `mn.select` for status, inline `mn.date_input` with "Heute" action icon, copy-to-clipboard action icon in `_booking_number`).
  - Toolbar: `alloq_project/components/project_toolbar.py` (`segmented`, `toolbar_search`, `icon_button("panel-right", ...)`, `primary_button`).
  - List state mixin: `alloq_project/states/project_list_state.py` (`FILTERS`, `STATUS_TONES`, `inspected_id`, `inspector_open` as `rx.LocalStorage`, `show_inspector`, grouped row computed vars).
  - Create modal: `add_project_modal` in `alloq_project/components/project_overview.py`; shared parts `modal_form_layout`, `modal_footer` in `alloq_commons/components/modal_layout.py`.
- Shared UI parts: `alloq_commons/components/list_view.py`, `toolbar.py`, `formatters.py` (`de_number`), `shell.py` (`app_page`). Colors only from `alloq_commons.theme`.
- Entity/repo pattern: `alloq_commons/entities/department.py`, `alloq_commons/repositories/department_repository.py` (`BaseRepository[XEntity, AsyncSession]`, module singleton). Money columns use `Numeric` + `Decimal` like `alloq_commons/entities/price_list.py`. Enum-as-German-label pattern: `ProjectStateEnum(enum.StrEnum)` in `alloq_commons/entities/project.py`.
- Package template: `components/alloq-team/pyproject.toml` and its `src/alloq_team/{components,services,states,pages.py}` + `tests/` layout.
- Roles and access: `alloq_commons/roles.py` (`PROJECT_MANAGER_ROLE` id 1, `EMPLOYEE_ROLE` id 2, `ALL_ROLES`), `alloq_commons/access.py` (`CAN_EDIT`, `editor_only`, `_guard`, `requires_editor`, `ACCESS_LEVEL_ATTR`). The word "editor" is already used there for admin + project manager, so the new role is named `offer_editor`.
- Sidebar: `app/components/sidebar.py` (`PLANNING_ITEMS`, `VIEWER_ROUTES`, `_guarded_nav_item`). Registration: `app/app.py`.
- Guards: `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` (`PACKAGES`, `EDITOR_PACKAGES`, `UI_ONLY_HANDLERS`, access-level checks), `tests/test_component_boundaries.py`.
- Migrations: current head is `bd91ef12ac34` (`alembic/versions/2026_10_19_department_highlight.py`); `alembic/env.py` imports `alloq_commons.entities` to register tables; new revisions go first in `KNOWN_REVISIONS` in `app/desktop/schema.py`.
- Root `pyproject.toml` lists every package in `dependencies`, `[tool.uv.sources]`, `[[tool.bumpversion.files]]`, pytest `testpaths` and coverage `source`.

## Requirements

### 1. Package scaffold
1. Create `components/alloq-offer/pyproject.toml` (copy `alloq-team`, name `alloq-offer`, same version, dependency `alloq-commons`, wheel package `src/alloq_offer`).
2. Layout: `src/alloq_offer/{__init__.py, entities.py, models.py, repository.py, services/, states/, components/, pages.py}` and `tests/`. Split into sub-modules only if a file grows large.
3. Register in root `pyproject.toml`: `dependencies`, `[tool.uv.sources]`, a `[[tool.bumpversion.files]]` block, `testpaths`, coverage `source`. Run `uv sync` (via `task sync`).

### 2. Data layer (in `alloq_offer`)
4. Enums (`enum.StrEnum`, values are the German labels shown in the UI):
   - `OfferStateEnum`: `NEW = "Neu"`, `IN_PROGRESS = "In Bearbeitung"`, `SENT = "Versendet"`.
   - `CustomerIndustryUnit`: values are the codes `CP, FS, U, P, H, IMC`, plus a module constant `CIU_LABELS` mapping code → label: "Consumer Services - CP", "Financial Services - FS", "Utilities - U", "Public - P", "Health - H", "Industrial Midcaps - IMC".
5. `OfferEntity(Entity, Base)`, table `offers`:
   | Column | Type | Rule |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | `title` | String(255) | required |
   | `customer` | String(255) | required |
   | `person_days` | Numeric(8,2) | required, ≥ 0 ("PT") |
   | `risk_buffer_days` | Numeric(8,2) | required, ≥ 0, default 0 ("Risikopuffer (PT)") |
   | `production_cost` | Numeric(12,2) | required, ≥ 0 ("Herstellkosten (HK)", €) |
   | `recommended_price` | Numeric(12,2) | required, ≥ 0 ("Empfohlener VK", €) |
   | `key_accounter` | String(255) | required, free text |
   | `ciu` | String(10) | required, one of the CIU codes |
   | `sharepoint_url` | String(2048) | optional |
   | `sent_date` | Date | optional |
   | `state` | String(20) | required, default `Neu` |
   | `archived` | Boolean | not null, default false, `server_default=false()` |
   `to_dict()` returns every field plus `id`, `created`, `updated`.
6. Pydantic `Offer` read model and `OfferCreate` write model with `Field` limits matching the columns; `sharepoint_url` must be empty or start with `http://` or `https://`; `ciu` and `state` validated against the enums; strings stripped and non-empty where required.
7. `OfferRepository(BaseRepository[OfferEntity, AsyncSession])` with `find_all_ordered()` (newest `updated` first) and module singleton `offer_repo`. No delete method is used anywhere.
8. Make the table known to Alembic: `alloq_offer` must register `OfferEntity` on `Base.metadata`, and `alembic/env.py` imports `alloq_offer.entities` next to `alloq_commons.entities`. Make sure the SQLite test setup also sees the table.
9. Hand-written migration `alembic/versions/2026_10_21_offers.py`: new revision id, `down_revision = "bd91ef12ac34"`, `op.create_table("offers", ...)` with all columns and an index on `state`; real `downgrade()` dropping the table. Add the revision as first entry of `KNOWN_REVISIONS` in `app/desktop/schema.py`.

### 3. Pure services (`alloq_offer/services/`)
10. `apply_state_change(state: str, sent_date: date | None, new_state: str, today: date) -> date | None`: when `new_state` is `Versendet` and `sent_date` is empty, return `today`; otherwise return `sent_date` unchanged (moving back to Neu/In Bearbeitung keeps the date). Used by create, edit and the inline status select.
11. Derived values for the inspector: `total_days = person_days + risk_buffer_days`, `margin_pct = (recommended_price - production_cost) / recommended_price * 100` (None when VK is 0). Plain functions, unit-tested.
12. Filtering/grouping helpers: search over title, customer and key accounter (case-insensitive); filter segments; sort by column.

### 4. Roles and access (small, shared touchpoints in `alloq_commons`)
13. `alloq_commons/roles.py`: add `OFFER_EDITOR_ROLE = Role(id=3, name="offer_editor", label="Angebote", description="Lesen und Bearbeiten der Angebote")` and append it to `ALL_ROLES` so it appears in user management.

name: alloq-implementation
description: Alloq house rules for writing code in this repo - architecture map, layer placement, handler authorization contract, German UI text, test recipes and the definition of done. Load this before writing or changing any code in the Alloq repo, for every implementation task - add a feature, fix a bug, refactor, add a field, entity, page, state, handler, service or component, write an Alembic migration, or add tests - even when the request looks small or does not mention architecture. Use it alongside the generic skills (python-coding, python-clean-code, reflex-state-and-architecture, reflex-testing-state, appkit-commons, appkit-mantine-reference); this skill says how Alloq applies them.
---

# Alloq implementation

Alloq is a Reflex 0.10 app for resource and project planning. The generic skills
explain Python, Reflex and appkit in general. This skill is the Alloq layer: where
code goes in this repo, which guards it must keep green, and how Alloq tests look.
When the two disagree, this skill wins, because it describes the code as it is.

Stack: Python 3.14, uv workspace (`UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv.mac`), Reflex 0.10,
appkit-* (`appkit_mantine as mn`, `appkit_commons`, `appkit_user`, `appkit_ui`),
SQLAlchemy 2.0 async, Pydantic, Alembic, PostgreSQL in production and SQLite in tests.
UI text is German. Code, comments and log messages are English.

## Workflow for every task

1. **Search memory** for the feature words and for error text you see. Past sessions
   stored traps here (for example the mixin rule and the umlaut escaping in tests).
2. **Read the reference code of the layer you touch** before writing. The canonical
   slice is departments (see the architecture map). Copying its shape is faster and
   keeps reviews short.
3. **Plan the smallest diff.** Change the layers the task needs and nothing else. Do
   not move files, rename folders or refactor neighbours unless asked.
4. **Write or adjust the test first**, in the test file of the package you change.
   For a bug, first write a test that fails because of the bug. Run the touched test
   files once before changing code, so you know which failures were already there;
   report those instead of fixing them inside the same diff.
5. **Implement.**
6. **Run the gates**: `task format && task lint && task typecheck && task test`.
   For a quick loop run only the touched test files with
   `uv run pytest <file> -q`, but run `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` whenever
   you add or change an event handler.
7. **Check file sizes**: `python .claude/skills/alloq-implementation/scripts/check_file_sizes.py`.
8. **Update memory** with any new trap or decision that the code itself does not show.

## Architecture map

Host app `app/` (entry `app/app.py`, admin pages `app/pages/*.py`, sidebar in
`app/components/sidebar.py`) plus uv workspace packages in `components/`:

| Package | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `alloq-commons` | shared kernel: entities, models, repositories, shared services, shared UI, `theme.py`, `roles.py`, `access.py` |
| `alloq-project` | projects and planning: `components/`, `services/`, `states/`, `pages.py` |
| `alloq-dashboard` | dashboard and portfolio: same layout, `models.py` for card payloads |
| `alloq-team` | team overview and employees: same layout |

Layers, in the order data flows (paths for departments under
`components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/`):

| Layer | Where | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entity | `entities/department.py` | `class XEntity(Entity, Base)`, `to_dict()` with every field |
| Model | `models/department.py` | Pydantic read model plus `XCreate` write model with `Field` limits |
| Repository | `repositories/department_repository.py` | `BaseRepository[XEntity, AsyncSession]`, `model_class`, module singleton `x_repo` |
| Service | `<pkg>/services/*.py` | pure functions and dataclasses; DB loading kept in `*_inputs.py` or loader functions |
| State | `state/department_states.py` | `rx.State`, `rx.Field` vars, `@rx.event` handlers |

# Refined prompt: KI-Angebotswerkstatt in `alloq-offer` — multiphase plan (Etappe 0 + 1)

> Load `alloq-implementation` first in **every** phase, then `appkit-mantine-reference` before any `mn.*` component you have not used in this task, `reflex-state-and-architecture` / `reflex-testing-state` for states, `ai:building-pydantic-ai-agents` for the AI layer. Follow the test-first workflow and the definition of done of `alloq-implementation`. One phase = one reviewable PR. Do not start a phase before the previous one is green.

## Task

Build the AI-supported offer workshop described in `spec/ki-angebotswerkstatt.md` (German, 785 lines; read §5–§14, §17, §18 before each phase) **inside the existing package `components/alloq-offer`**. For an existing offer, an `offer_editor` adds customer sources (pasted text, EML, TXT, DOCX, PDF, PPTX, audio), the app extracts them, an LLM proposes a **User Story Map with simple stories (no acceptance criteria)**, the user edits map, stories and scope, the app drafts the chapters of the bound Word template, the user edits chapters in the browser, rule checks plus an AI review produce findings, and the app exports an editable DOCX (draft or final) into the existing QUO template layout.

The plan covers spec Etappe 0 (template proof) and Etappe 1 (first end-to-end version) in detail. Etappe 2/3 are only listed under "Out of scope".

## Decisions already made (do not re-ask)

| Topic | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Placement | Extend `alloq-offer` (import `alloq_offer`). New code lives in a sub-package `alloq_offer/workshop/`. Depends only on `alloq-commons` + appkit, never on `app` or other alloq packages. |
| UI stack | Reflex + `appkit_mantine` (not Next.js as the spec suggests). Rich text via `mn.rich_text_editor` (Tiptap wrapper in `appkit_mantine/tiptap.py`). |
| LLM | Azure OpenAI through **pydantic-ai** (`OpenAIChatModel` + `AzureProvider`) behind a narrow port. Tests use pydantic-ai `TestModel` / `FunctionModel` via `Agent.override`, never the network. |
| Access | Whole workshop (sources, transcripts, map, chapters, findings, exports) read **and** write only for role `offer_editor` (`OFFER_EDITOR_ROLE`, `@requires_offer_editor`). Offer list stays readable for all. No per-offer ownership in Etappe 1. |
| Storage | A `BlobStore` protocol; first implementation stores bytes in Postgres (`offer_blobs`, `LargeBinary`, deduplicated by SHA-256) so server and desktop share files. Azure Blob is a later adapter. |

entities.py / models.py          # split into entities/ and models/ packages once > ~400 lines
repositories/                    # BaseRepository[XEntity, AsyncSession] + module singletons
storage.py                       # BlobStore protocol + DbBlobStore
jobs/                            # job entity helpers, claim/lease/retry, runner, handlers registry
extraction/                      # one parser per kind: text, eml, docx, pdf, pptx, audio
ai/                              # pydantic-ai agents, output schemas, prompt files, settings
services/                        # pure logic: map ops, story validation, scope, checks, diff, snapshot
content/                         # canonical content tree schema + editor HTML <-> tree converter
export/                          # template package loader, docx renderer, manifest
templates/quo_v1/                # chapters.yaml, rules.yaml, layout.docx (prepared copy)
states/                          # one state per tab; mixins for list logic
components/                      # sources, map, briefing, chapters, checks, export panels
pages.py                         # create_offer_workshop_page(sidebar) -> /offers/[offer_id]/werkstatt
```

UI text German; code, comments, logs English; `logger.debug` default, no f-strings in logger calls, never log source content or prompts (spec §15).

---

## Phase 0 — Template proof and content contract (spec Etappe 0, §6, §10.3, §13)

Goal: prove the QUO template can be filled with editable content before any AI work.

1. Inventory the QUO DOCX with a small script under `scripts/` (headings, styles, tables, numbering, TOC field, content controls, header/footer). Write the result to `docs/features/offer-workshop-template.md` (chapter list, which parts are static, which become generated, style names to use).
2. Define the **template package** `templates/quo_v1/`:
   - `chapters.yaml`: stable chapter keys, title, level, required flag, guiding question, content rules, order. First functional chapter is `story_map` (projection, not free text), then the QUO chapters (management_summary, loesung, leistungsumfang, mitwirkung, rahmenbedingungen, projektabwicklung, laufzeit, verguetung, annahmen_risiken …) per inventory; static legal chapters (Rechtlicher Hinweis, Rechtliche Bestimmungen, Bindefrist, Unterschriften) stay fixed text.
   - `layout.docx`: a prepared copy of the QUO file with `docxtpl` placeholders / subdoc anchors per chapter; customer data removed.
   - `rules.yaml`: per-chapter required info and checks (used in Phase 6).
   - A Pydantic `TemplatePackage` model + loader with a `version` string; compatibility check (every chapter key has an anchor in `layout.docx`).
3. Define the **canonical content tree** (`content/schema.py`, Pydantic, discriminated union): `paragraph` (inline runs: text, bold, italic), `heading` (levels 3–4 only inside a chapter), `bullet_list`, `ordered_list`, `table` (header row + rows of plain inline runs), `bound_value` (reference to a structured field, e.g. `offer.recommended_price`). Every block has a stable `block_id`. Anything else is rejected with a German validation message.
4. Word renderer (`export/docx_renderer.py`) using `docxtpl` + `python-docx`: maps each block to template styles, renders the story map as per-activity tables plus a story catalogue (key, title, sentence, scope), resolves bound values, adds no external resources. Unsupported blocks raise a typed error (no silent loss).
5. Reference export test: render a fixture with long text, nested lists, a wide table, umlauts/special chars (`<>&„“€`), many activities; assert structurally with python-docx (chapter order, headings, table cells, styles, TOC field present). Write the file to `tmp_path` and keep one sample under `docs/` for manual Word check.

Deps: `uv add --package alloq-offer docxtpl python-docx`.
Done: tests green; user opens the sample DOCX in Word and confirms layout (gate before Phase 3).

## Phase 1 — Workspace foundation, storage and job runner (spec §8.6, §14.2, §15)

1. Entities + one migration `2026_10_xx_offer_workshop_base.py` (down_revision `a2b3c4d5e6f7`):
   - `offer_workspaces` (offer_id unique FK → offers, RESTRICT because offers are never deleted; template_key, template_version, vision, roles JSON, map_revision int, story_seq int, doc_state `Entwurf|In Prüfung|Final`, created_by).
   - `offer_blobs` (sha256 unique, size, mime, data LargeBinary).
   - `offer_jobs` (offer_id, kind, status `queued|running|succeeded|failed|cancelled`, idempotency_key unique, payload JSON, input_revisions JSON, attempts, max_attempts, run_after, lease_until, error_class, error_message (technical text only), result JSON, timestamps). Index on (status, run_after).
2. `BlobStore` protocol (`put(bytes, mime) -> blob_id`, `get(blob_id)`, `delete`) + `DbBlobStore`; size limit from config.
3. Job runner (`jobs/`): `enqueue(kind, offer_id, payload, idempotency_key)` returns existing job for the same key; `claim_next()` uses `SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` on Postgres (plain select on SQLite tests); lease + heartbeat; bounded retries with backoff for transient errors; results of expired/cancelled jobs are discarded; model/parser calls run **outside** DB transactions. Handlers register by `kind` (registry pattern).
4. Worker: an async loop started via `app.register_lifespan_task` in `app/app.py`, enabled by config `offer_workshop.worker_enabled` (YAML + `__` env override), bounded concurrency. Desktop and server may both run it safely thanks to SKIP LOCKED.
5. Config section in `configuration/config.yaml` for workshop (limits, worker, Azure OpenAI endpoint/deployments, secret refs `secret:azure_openai_api_key`), loaded via appkit config pattern (`appkit-commons` skill).
6. Page shell: `create_offer_workshop_page(sidebar)` route `/offers/[offer_id]/werkstatt`, gated with `requires_role(…, OFFER_EDITOR_ROLE.name)`; tabs `Story Map · Quellen · Briefing · Kapitel · Prüfung · Export`; entry from the offer inspector ("Werkstatt öffnen", offer_editor only). Opening creates the workspace lazily with the default template package. Empty map shows guiding questions, never invented content (spec §5.1, "Liegen noch keine Quellen vor").
7. Tests: repository, job claim/retry/lease/idempotency (SQLite), state open/create workspace, authorization classification, migration test, `KNOWN_REVISIONS`.

## Phase 2 — Sources and extraction (spec §5.2, §7)

1. Entities + migration: `offer_sources` (offer_id, kind `text|eml|txt|docx|pdf|pptx|audio`, title, filename, mime, blob_id, sha256, version, replaces_id, status `hochgeladen|in Verarbeitung|nutzbar|teilweise nutzbar|fehlgeschlagen|manuell nötig`, status_detail, included bool, revoked_at), `offer_source_blocks` (source_id, seq, anchor JSON {page|paragraph|table|slide|shape|note|start_ms/end_ms|message_id}, kind, speaker, text, gap flag + reason).
2. Upload via `mn.dropzone` / `rx.upload` (type and size whitelist, no macros executed, macro-enabled Office types rejected) and a "Text einfügen" modal. Identical sha256 on the same offer → no new version, no new job. Replacing a file creates a new version.
3. Parsers (`extraction/`, one module each, pure `bytes -> ExtractionResult`):
   - pasted text / TXT; EML via stdlib `email` (subject, date, sender, message-id, quoted chain and signature detection, attachments become their own sources).
   - DOCX via python-docx (paragraphs, tables; anchors by paragraph/table index).
   - PDF via `pypdf` (pages; pages without text layer → gap "OCR nötig", not silently skipped).
   - PPTX via `python-pptx` (slide no., text frames, tables, notes; picture shapes → gap "Bildinhalt nicht ausgewertet").
   - Audio (WAV/MP3/M4A) via a `Transcriber` port with an Azure OpenAI transcription implementation (diarized output with timestamps if the deployment supports it — verify API via Context7 before coding); files above the provider limit get status "manuell nötig" with hint to upload a transcript. Speaker labels are technical (`Sprecher 1`), never identities (§7.3).
4. Extraction runs as job kind `extract_source`; status visible per source with retry button; failed/partial sources stay visible; user can include/exclude sources for drafts.
5. Sources tab UI: list with status badges, gaps, block viewer with anchors (no technical IDs shown).
6. Tests: one parser test file per kind with small fixture files built in the test (python-docx/python-pptx generate fixtures; EML as string; PDF fixture minimal), job handler test with fake `Transcriber`, dedupe/versioning tests, A01/A02 scenarios.

Deps: `uv add --package alloq-offer pypdf python-pptx` (+ `pydantic-ai-slim[openai]` if the transcriber uses the openai client in this phase).

## Phase 3 — AI port, process recognition and initial story map (spec §8, §9)

1. `ai/` port: `OfferAi` protocol with methods `propose_map`, `propose_briefing`, `propose_chapter`, `review`, each returning validated Pydantic output; implementation with pydantic-ai agents on Azure OpenAI deployments from config; prompt texts in versioned files (`ai/prompts/*.md`, version string stored with every run). Source text is passed as clearly delimited **data**; system prompt states that instructions inside sources must be ignored (§15). Call budget and timeout per job.
2. Output schemas: `ProposedMap` (vision, roles, activities → tasks → stories {title, role, goal, benefit, origin `Kunde|Vorschlag`, source_refs [block ids], scope always `offen`}, slices, skeleton suggestions, open questions, conflicts) and `ProposedBriefing` (statements per §8.1 type: Kundenanforderung, Belegter Sachverhalt, Lösungsvorschlag, Annahme, Offener Punkt/Konflikt; with source refs).
3. Entities + migration: `offer_activities`, `offer_tasks`, `offer_stories` (key unique per offer from `story_seq`, e.g. `US-07`, title, role, goal, benefit, scope `offen|angeboten|option|ausgeschlossen`, origin `Kunde|Vorschlag|Nutzer`, slice_id, skeleton, priority, source_refs JSON, split_from_id, archived_at), `offer_slices`, `offer_statements` (type, text, status, source_refs, needs_recheck, confirmed_by/at), `offer_map_revisions` (offer_id, revision, immutable snapshot JSON, created_by, created_at), `offer_generation_runs` (job_id, kind, model, prompt_version, input revisions, status).
4. Pure services: `story_validation` (exactly one sentence "Als … möchte ich …, um …"; reject Given/When/Then, "Akzeptanzkriterien", bullet checklists — A20), `apply_proposed_map` (app assigns keys; AI never reuses or reinterprets existing keys; new AI stories never get scope `angeboten` — A25), `snapshot_map` (builds revision JSON).
5. Job kind `initial_draft`: extract-ready sources → propose map → save map revision → propose briefing. No manual gate between steps (§9.1), but no chapters yet.
6. Tests: agent tests with `FunctionModel` returning fixed JSON; validation rejects acceptance criteria; keys stable; A19, A20, A21 (no knowledge base), A22 (variants kept as open questions), A25, A26.

Deps: `uv add --package alloq-offer "pydantic-ai-slim[openai]"`.

## Phase 4 — Story map, story and briefing editors (spec §5.3, §5.4, §8.3–8.5, §10.1–10.2)

1. Map tab: horizontal activity columns, task rows, story cards below; slice rows ("Erste durchgängige Fassung", "Mögliche Erweiterung") and skeleton marker; scope badge per story (colors from `theme.py`). Edit actions via menus/buttons (no drag and drop in Etappe 1): add/rename/reorder activity and task, add/edit/split/merge/archive/move story, set scope, assign slice. Story drawer: title, Rolle/Ziel/Nutzen fields, live sentence preview, origin, source anchors, open questions.
2. Every map write uses optimistic concurrency: handler sends expected `map_revision`; mismatch → German conflict toast + reload, no overwrite (A08). Each saved change bumps `map_revision` and writes a snapshot; split keeps `split_from_id`; archived keys are never reused (A23).
3. Briefing tab: statements grouped by type, conflicts show both source anchors (A03), "Als fachliche Entscheidung bestätigen" is a separate explicit action (§8.7, A17).
4. Story/scope change marks dependent chapters `needs_review` (hook ready for Phase 5; A09, A27).
5. Map-level AI actions as jobs returning a **proposal** (compare + accept), e.g. "fehlende Prozessschritte vorschlagen", "Story aufteilen". Proposals bound to an older revision are shown as "veraltet" (A07).
6. Keep states ≤ ~400 lines: `MapState` + `MapEditMixin` + `StoryDrawerState`, list logic in mixins. Tests per handler incl. conflict and authorization.

## Phase 5 — Chapters, editor, revisions and proposals (spec §5.5, §9.4, §10.2–10.4)

1. Entities + migration: `offer_chapters` (offer_id, chapter_key, current_revision_id, protected, needs_review, review_reason), `offer_chapter_revisions` (chapter_id, number, content JSON = canonical tree, base_revision, map_revision, origin `manuell|KI übernommen`, author), `offer_proposals` (target chapter or map, job_id, content JSON, base revision, status `offen|übernommen|verworfen|veraltet`).
2. Converter `content/editor_io.py`: `mn.rich_text_editor` value ↔ canonical tree, restricted to the Phase 0 block set (check in `appkit-mantine-reference` whether the editor emits HTML or JSON; parse HTML with stdlib `html.parser`, drop nothing silently — unsupported markup → validation finding). Round-trip tests for every block type (A06). Editor toolbar limited to the supported marks.
3. Chapter tab layout per spec §10.1: chapter list (left), editor (center), context (right: linked stories, sources, assumptions, findings, revision info). `story_map` chapter is a read-only projection of the current map revision.
4. Autosave with expected base revision (debounced); visible save state; conflict → visible message, no overwrite (A08). Revision history with diff and restore.
5. Job kind `draft_chapters`: uses map revision + briefing + template guiding questions + profile (Software/AI/Agent/Data Science, §12.2) to propose chapters; closely related chapters may be drafted together. Results become proposals, never overwrite a manual or protected chapter (A07). "Vorschlag übernehmen" creates a new revision; it does not confirm business decisions (A17). Per-chapter AI instructions ("kürzen", "technischer formulieren", free prompt).
6. Tests: converter round-trip, revision conflict, stale proposal, protected chapter, needs_review after story change.

## Phase 6 — Commercial values, rule checks and AI review (spec §8.7, §11, §12.1)

1. Commercial fields: reuse offer fields (`person_days`, `risk_buffer_days`, `production_cost`, `recommended_price`) plus new workspace fields (currency, validity date, price required flag) and an explicit "Kalkulation bestätigen" action storing confirmed_by/at and the confirmed values. Chapters reference them only via `bound_value` blocks. Changing a confirmed value invalidates the confirmation and marks linked chapters (A09).
2. Entities + migration: `offer_findings` (offer_id, rule, severity `Blocker|Warnung|Hinweis`, source `Regel|KI`, target, revision refs, message, decision `offen|behoben|akzeptiert`, reason, decided_by/at).
3. Rule checks as pure functions over a snapshot (§11.1): required chapters present, map first and without acceptance criteria, every story assigned to task/activity, map/story revision matches chapters, no placeholders, statuses on requirements, price/sum consistency, free-text numbers that differ from bound values (A18), sources still allowed (revoked source → finding).
4. AI review job (§11.2) → findings with concrete reference, never edits content, no global score.
5. Prüfung tab: findings list with filters, decision with mandatory reason where the rule allows acceptance.
6. Tests: each rule with pass/fail fixtures; A04, A05, A11, A15, A18.

## Phase 7 — Snapshots and Word export (spec §5.6, §11.3, §13)

1. Entities + migration: `offer_snapshots` (immutable JSON of map revision, stories, chapters, bound values, template version), `offer_exports` (snapshot_id, kind `Entwurf|Final`, template_version, exporter_version, blob_id, sha256, status, error, created_by).
2. Export flow as job `export_docx`: unsaved browser changes block export; server builds snapshot → validates kind (final requires: required chapters, no open blockers, confirmed commercials if the template demands a price, user confirmation of the whole snapshot) → renders with Phase 0 renderer → structural check → stores blob + manifest. Draft shows a visible draft marker and open points; final hides internal review metadata but keeps customer-relevant assumptions, exclusions and obligations (§11.3).
3. Export tab: list of exports with kind, revision, date, author; download returns the stored bytes exactly (`rx.download`); failure keeps state and shows retry (A13). No sync back from Word (A16).
4. Template binding: workspace stores template version; a new package version does not change existing offers (A14).
5. Tests: final blocked with reasons (A11), draft allowed, manifest checksum, download equals stored blob, A12, A24.

## Phase 8 — Hardening, docs and acceptance matrix (spec §14.2, §15, §18, §19)

1. Source revocation/deletion: blocks further use immediately, marks dependent content, deletes blobs and blocks (§15).
2. Telemetry: job durations, status, error classes, token/cost counters per phase in logs (no content, no prompts).
3. Authorization sweep (A10): every workshop handler and download path checks `offer_editor`; non-editors get no workspace data, not even via direct URL.
4. Acceptance matrix: `components/alloq-offer/tests/test_workshop_acceptance.py` mapping A01–A27 to tests (or to the phase test that covers them); list any case not automatable.
5. Docs: `docs/features/offer-workshop.md` (user flow, stories, architecture diagram per `docs-diagram-style`), update `docs/features/offers.md` and `README.md`. Memory updates for new traps.

## Cross-phase requirements

- Tests first; coverage ≥ 80 % for non-Reflex classes and states; `task format && task lint && task typecheck && task test` green after each phase; `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` run after every handler change; file size check.
- Every migration: hand-written, tested in `tests/test_migrations.py`, added first to `KNOWN_REVISIONS`, imported in `alembic/env.py`. The user applies migrations; do not run alembic against `PROFILES=local`.
- Secrets only via config secret refs / Key Vault; `SecretStr.get_secret_value()`.
- No content, prompts or credentials in logs; parameterized logging only.
- Stories never get acceptance criteria — at generation, regeneration, review and export.

## Success criteria (end of Phase 8)

- With `worker_enabled` and an Azure OpenAI deployment configured, an `offer_editor` can: open the workshop from an offer, add an EML, a DOCX, a PDF, a PPTX and an audio file, see per-source status and gaps, get an initial story map + briefing, edit map/stories/scope, generate and edit chapters, resolve findings, and download a draft and a final DOCX that opens in Word with the QUO layout, the story map as first functional content and editable chapters.
- A user without `offer_editor` cannot reach any workshop data.
- All A01–A27 cases are covered by tests or documented manual checks.

## Out of scope (Etappe 2/3 and later)

Company knowledge base / Azure AI Search, effort estimation by AI, more templates and profiles beyond quo_v1, MSG files, mailbox/meeting/SharePoint/CRM connectors, OCR and visual slide analysis (Etappe 1 only flags these gaps), drag and drop map editing, live collaboration, per-offer member permissions, Word preview and Word re-import, Azure Blob adapter, four-eyes approval.

You approved the plan. It is at `/Users/jens/.claude/plans/nested-booping-cat.md` and is written as a prompt that another session can work through one phase at a time. No code has been written yet.

**Decisions it is built on:**
- **Location:** a new `workshop/` sub-package inside `alloq-offer`, built with Reflex and `mn.rich_text_editor`. The spec's suggested Next.js stack is not used.
- **AI model:** Azure OpenAI through pydantic-ai. Tests use pydantic-ai's fake test models and never call the real service.
- **Access:** only users with the `offer_editor` role can see or change anything in the workshop. The offer list stays readable for everyone.

content.text:
I made three layout concepts on one design canvas: [Angebotswerkstatt Prototypen](https://claude.ai/artifact/SqvwnLbKttsfEL7XwnTcYX).

They use the current macOS-blue Alloq look from `theme.py` (colors, system font, card shadows, radii). I did not use the Alloq design system, because it still has the old teal colors. All three show the same example from spec §16, the Kundenanfragen offer with stories ANF-01 to ANF-07. The mockups are static, and I haven't opened them in a browser to check them.

- **A · Arbeitsbereich mit Tabs:** this follows the plan most closely. The normal Alloq sidebar is on the left. The workspace has tabs: Story Map, Quellen, Briefing, Kapitel, Prüfung and Export.
  - The map is a full grid of activities, tasks and slice rows. Story cards show the scope, the walking skeleton marker and AI suggestions drawn with a dashed border.
  - A story inspector on the right has Rolle, Ziel and Nutzen fields with a preview of the full sentence, a scope switch and links to the sources.
  - A list of open questions sits below the map, and a status bar shows the save state, blockers and the export buttons.
- **B · Cockpit:** this is the layout drawn in spec §10.1.
  - A compact map band at the top stays visible and can be collapsed.
  - Below it are three panes: the chapter list with a status per chapter, the rich text editor and a context panel. The context panel shows the linked stories, check findings, the AI proposal and source locations.
  - The editor shows the case where the map changed: a banner says the chapter is out of date, the sentence that conflicts with the scope is highlighted, and the effort appears as an unconfirmed linked value.
- **C · Dokumentfluss:** the work happens on the offer document itself.
  - A progress row across the top lets you jump to any step: Quellen, Story Map, Briefing, Kapitel, Prüfung, Export.
  - The left side shows the document outline. In the middle is the page as it will look in Word, with the map as a table, an AI change shown inline to accept or reject, and an unsupported claim marked in the text.
  - A panel on the right shows findings, a briefing conflict with both sources, source statuses and export. Final export is locked while there is a blocker.

The canvas is private. Other people can only open the link after you share it from the page's Share menu.

content.text:
I added a new row called "Kombination A + C – Entwurf in einem Durchlauf" to the canvas: [Angebotswerkstatt Prototypen](https://claude.ai/artifact/SqvwnLbKttsfEL7XwnTcYX). It has two clickable boards. I haven't clicked through them in Play mode yet, so a broken button is possible.

**1 · Entwurf erzeugen und Story Map anpassen**
- **Start:** you choose which sources to use (EML, audio, PPTX, PDF). Gaps such as unanalysed images or a page that needs OCR are shown. There is one button, "Entwurf aus 3 Quellen erzeugen", and an option to start the draft automatically when new sources become usable.
- **One run, no stops in between:** a progress list shows the steps: analyse sources, find processes and roles, build the story map, write the briefing, propose a scope, draft all 9 chapters, run the checks, create the Word draft.
- **Result:** a summary card says the first draft is done, with buttons to download the Word draft and to view the chapters. Below it is a short list called "Braucht deine Entscheidung" with only what the AI must not decide alone:
  - confirm the proposed scope (one click marks the 5 skeleton stories as offered)
  - settle the Cloud versus On-Premises conflict
  - confirm effort and price, which is only needed for the final version
- **Optional editing of the map:**
  - Activities can be renamed, moved left or right, added, and removed if they have no stories.
  - Each activity has an editable task.
  - You can add and rename release slices ("Umsetzungsschnitte").
  - Every cell has "+ Story", and new stories get the next free ANF number.
  - Clicking a story opens a side panel for Rolle, Ziel and Nutzen, with the full sentence shown live. It also has the scope, a move to another activity or slice, split and archive.
  - "Fehlende Schritte vorschlagen" adds a dashed AI suggestion that you accept or reject. It only gets an ANF number when you accept it.
  - Any edit raises the revision number and shows "Kapitel neu vorschlagen". Chapters you edited by hand are not overwritten.
- In the Tweaks panel, the "startPhase" setting lets you start the board directly with the finished draft.

**2 · Kapitel im Dokument**

This board has A's frame and C's document view:
- The chapter outline is on the left and the offer page in Word layout is in the middle. The story map appears there as a table you can only change in the map editor, and the Management Summary text can be edited directly.
- The review's AI proposal to replace the unsupported promise ("garantiert um die Hälfte") can be accepted or rejected. If you accept it, the check finding disappears.
- The right side shows check findings, the stories and sources linked to the chapter, a switch to protect the chapter from AI changes, and export. The final version stays locked while findings are open.

The saved plan in `spec/plans/ki-angebotswerkstatt.md` doesn't match this yet. Its Phase 3 first draft stops after the map and the briefing, so it needs updating to the one-click full draft and this layout.

**Each chapter has a type.** The type shows as a badge on the chapter heading and as a short label in the outline:

| Type | In the document | Settings on the right |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Story Map** | Graphical map, at most once per document | Show or hide extensions, link to the map editor |

| **Tabelle** | Header row plus cells you edit directly | Columns; button to add a row |
| **Kalkulation** | Effort and price as linked values, marked "nicht bestätigt" until confirmed | Note that the final version is locked; link to the calculation |

Every chapter can be renamed, moved up or down, and removed unless it is required. Base directory for this skill: /Users/jens/Workspace/work/alloq/.claude/skills/alloq-implementation

# Alloq implementation

Alloq is a Reflex 0.10 app for resource and project planning. The generic skills
explain Python, Reflex and appkit in general. This skill is the Alloq layer: where
code goes in this repo, which guards it must keep green, and how Alloq tests look.
When the two disagree, this skill wins, because it describes the code as it is.

Stack: Python 3.14, uv workspace (`UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv.mac`), Reflex 0.10,
appkit-* (`appkit_mantine as mn`, `appkit_commons`, `appkit_user`, `appkit_ui`),
SQLAlchemy 2.0 async, Pydantic, Alembic, PostgreSQL in production and SQLite in tests.
UI text is German. Code, comments and log messages are English.

## Workflow for every task

1. **Search memory** for the feature words and for error text you see. Past sessions
   stored traps here (for example the mixin rule and the umlaut escaping in tests).
2. **Read the reference code of the layer you touch** before writing. The canonical
   slice is departments (see the architecture map). Copying its shape is faster and
   keeps reviews short.
3. **Plan the smallest diff.** Change the layers the task needs and nothing else. Do
   not move files, rename folders or refactor neighbours unless asked.
4. **Write or adjust the test first**, in the test file of the package you change.
   For a bug, first write a test that fails because of the bug. Run the touched test
   files once before changing code, so you know which failures were already there;
   report those instead of fixing them inside the same diff.
5. **Implement.**
6. **Run the gates**: `task format && task lint && task typecheck && task test`.
   For a quick loop run only the touched test files with
   `uv run pytest <file> -q`, but run `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` whenever
   you add or change an event handler.
7. **Check file sizes**: `python .claude/skills/alloq-implementation/scripts/check_file_sizes.py`.
8. **Update memory** with any new trap or decision that the code itself does not show.

## Architecture map

Host app `app/` (entry `app/app.py`, admin pages `app/pages/*.py`, sidebar in
`app/components/sidebar.py`) plus uv workspace packages in `components/`:

| Package | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `alloq-commons` | shared kernel: entities, models, repositories, shared services, shared UI, `theme.py`, `roles.py`, `access.py` |
| `alloq-project` | projects and planning: `components/`, `services/`, `states/`, `pages.py` |
| `alloq-dashboard` | dashboard and portfolio: same layout, `models.py` for card payloads |
| `alloq-team` | team overview and employees: same layout |

Layers, in the order data flows (paths for departments under
`components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/`):

| Layer | Where | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entity | `entities/department.py` | `class XEntity(Entity, Base)`, `to_dict()` with every field |
| Model | `models/department.py` | Pydantic read model plus `XCreate` write model with `Field` limits |
| Repository | `repositories/department_repository.py` | `BaseRepository[XEntity, AsyncSession]`, `model_class`, module singleton `x_repo` |
| Service | `<pkg>/services/*.py` | pure functions and dataclasses; DB loading kept in `*_inputs.py` or loader functions |
| State | `state/department_states.py` | `rx.State`, `rx.Field` vars, `@rx.event` handlers |
| Component | `components/department.py` | plain functions returning `rx.Component`, built from `mn.*` and shared parts |
| Page | `app/pages/departments.py` or `<pkg>/pages.py` | page factory `create_x_page(sidebar, route, title)` using `app_page` |
| Registration | `app/app.py` | call the factory with `sidebar()`; add a sidebar entry if needed |
| Migration | `alembic/versions/YYYY_MM_DD_<topic>.py` | hand-written, real `downgrade()` |

Dependency direction: feature packages import `alloq_commons` and appkit, never
`app` (`tests/test_component_boundaries.py` fails otherwise). Feature packages do not
import each other unless that import already exists. `app` may import everything.

`alloq_commons` has both `state/` (departments, roles) and `states/` (holidays). Put
new code next to its closest neighbour and do not merge the folders unasked.

Details, snippets and the background-load pattern: `references/architecture.md`.

## Where does this code belong?

- **Pure calculation** (scores, sums, sorting, grouping, labels) goes into a service
  function or a small dataclass, testable without a database. Examples:
  `alloq_dashboard/services/resource_path.py`, `alloq_project/services/project_sorting.py`.
- **Database reads and writes** go through a repository method, or a loader function
  such as `load_departments()` or `portfolio_inputs.py`. States do not build SQL.
- **UI state** (open dialogs, filters, toggles, selection) lives in the state. When the
  state file is large, put new vars and handlers into a mixin
  (`class XListState(rx.State, mixin=True)`), never into a substate; substates break
  tests that create the state on its own.
- **Rendering** goes into function components that read state vars. No logic beyond
  `rx.cond` / `rx.foreach` and formatting.
- **A value both the UI and a test need** (labels, messages, column lists) becomes a
  module constant, so tests can assert on it.

## Security: the handler authorization contract

Access levels (`alloq_commons.access`): admins may do everything; the project
manager role may read and edit every planning page (dashboard, planning, projects,
team) but not the administration; the employee role may only read planning and
projects. Page guards (`admin_only=True`, `editor_only`, `viewer_only`) only hide
the page. Event handlers run over the websocket for anyone with a session, so every
handler protects itself. `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` enforces this for all
states in the four packages. For each new or changed handler pick exactly one case:

1. **Reads or writes data in a planning package** (`alloq_dashboard`,
   `alloq_project`, `alloq_team`, `SidebarState`) → `@rx.event` then
   `@requires_editor` from `alloq_commons.access`. This is the default; the guard
   test rejects `@requires_admin` there.
1b. **Administration state** (`DepartmentState`, `RoleState`, `HolidayState`,
   `DatabaseAccessState`, listed in `ADMIN_STATES`) → `@requires_admin` from
   `appkit_user.authentication.decorators`.
2. **Read-only load the employee role may also run** → `@requires_viewer` from
   `alloq_commons.access`, and add the name to `VIEWER_HANDLERS`. It must not write.
3. **Only changes UI state** (open/close, set filter, toggle) → no decorator, add the
   name to `UI_ONLY_HANDLERS["<ConcreteState>"]`. The test scans its source and the
   `self.` helpers it calls for DB markers (`get_asyncdb_session`, `_repo.`,
   `aggregation.`, ...), so a UI-only handler must not touch a repository or session.
4. **Background handler** (`@rx.event(background=True)`) → guard decorators are not
   allowed (they need the state lock). Check edit rights inside `async with self`
   through `_CardLoadMixin._run_card_load` (`_can_edit`) and list it in
   `INLINE_ADMIN_CHECK`.

Edit controls in the planning UI go inside `editor_only(...)` or use
`disabled=~CAN_EDIT`; `admin_only(...)` is for administration only.

Handlers defined in a mixin are listed under the concrete state that mixes it in
(`TeamState`, `ProjectState`, `PlanningStore`), because the test skips mixins.
Remove allowlist entries when you delete or guard a handler; stale entries fail too.
Run the test after every handler change.

## Style that ruff does not catch

- German UI strings, including toasts: `rx.toast.error("Fehler beim Erstellen der
  Abteilung.", position="top-right")`. English for code, comments, docstrings, logs.
- `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` per module; `%s` arguments, never f-strings
  in log calls; `logger.exception(...)` in the final `except Exception` of a handler.
- Handler error shape: `ValidationError` → German hint, `IntegrityError` → duplicate
  message, `Exception` → `logger.exception` plus a generic German error toast.
- Colors, radii and shadows only from `alloq_commons.theme` (`theme.CARD`,
  `theme.TEXT_MUTED`, `theme.BLUE[6]`, ...). The theme is macOS blue; ignore the old
  teal design artifact.
- Use `mn.*` components. Load `appkit-mantine-reference` before using one you have
  not used in this task; its props are not in your training data.
- HTML attributes on `mn` inputs: `max_length=20` turns into CSS and limits nothing.
  Use `custom_attrs={"maxLength": 20}` for the browser limit, and keep the real check
  in the write model (`Field(max_length=20)`).
- State vars: `name: rx.Field[T] = rx.field(default)`; lists use
  `rx.field(default_factory=list)`. Type hints on every function, including tests.
- Prefer shared parts over new ones: `modal_form_layout`, `modal_footer`,
  `delete_dialog`, `toolbar_search`, `primary_button`, `section`, `app_page`,
  `window_toolbar`, `de_number`.

## Testing standards

Coverage must stay at 80 % or more (branch coverage, `fail_under = 80`). Put tests in
the package that owns the code: `components/<pkg>/tests/test_<feature>.py`. App-level
tests and the guards live in `tests/`.

- **Entity/model**: `to_dict()` keys, `XCreate` rejects bad input.
- **Service**: plain unit tests with hand-built inputs, no mocks needed.
- **State**: create the state directly, patch `MODULE.x_repo` and
  `MODULE.get_asyncdb_session`, fake the admin with `_as_admin`, and drive handlers
  with `_run`, which returns the toast text. Copy the helpers from
  `components/alloq-commons/tests/test_departments.py`.
- **Component**: render with `str(component())` and assert on var names or module
  constants. `str()` escapes umlauts (`ä` becomes `\u00e4`), so assert on the constant.
- **Migration with data changes**: add a test in `tests/test_migrations.py` that runs
  the migration offline on SQLite.

Recipes and snippets: `references/testing.md`.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Test written first; new behaviour and the bug case are covered
- [ ] `task format && task lint && task typecheck && task test` all green
- [ ] `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` and `tests/test_component_boundaries.py` green
- [ ] Every new handler has its guard or its allowlist entry
- [ ] New migration is hand-written, uses `op.batch_alter_table` for column changes,
      has a real `downgrade()`, and its revision is added to `KNOWN_REVISIONS` in
      `app/desktop/schema.py`
- [ ] No touched file grew past 1000 lines; files already over it did not grow
      without reason (see `references/pitfalls.md`)
- [ ] German UI text, theme tokens, no `print`, no f-strings in logs
- [ ] Memory updated with new traps or decisions

Per change type (new field, new handler, new page, new service, bug fix):
`references/checklists.md`. Known traps: `references/pitfalls.md`.

## Which generic skill for what

| Need | Skill |
| --- | --- |
| Python style, logging, typing, design patterns | `python-coding`, `python-clean-code` |
| Reflex state design, events, background tasks | `reflex-state-and-architecture`, `reflex-docs` |
| Writing state tests in general | `reflex-testing-state` |
| Config, service registry, repositories, column types | `appkit-commons` |
| Any `mn.*` component or prop | `appkit-mantine-reference` |
| Shrinking a big file you touched | `code-cleanup` |

They can then confirm the scope, resolve the listed decisions, optionally edit the map on its own screen and the typed chapters in the document view, and download a final DOCX that opens in Word with the QUO layout, the written stories and editable chapters (no map graphic).

206	- All A01–A27 cases are covered by tests or documented manual checks.

export UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv.mac && mkdir -p scripts && cat > scripts/inventory_docx.py <<'EOF'
"""Print an inventory of a DOCX template: paragraphs, styles, tables, fields."""

import sys
from pathlib import Path

from docx import Document
from docx.oxml.ns import qn


def main(path: str) -> None:
    doc = Document(path)
    body = doc.element.body
    index = 0
    for child in body.iterchildren():
        tag = child.tag.split("}")[1]
        if tag == "p":
            para = doc.paragraphs[index] if index < len(doc.paragraphs) else None
            index += 1
            style = child.find(qn("w:pPr") + "/" + qn("w:pStyle"))
            style_id = style.get(qn("w:val")) if style is not None else "-"
            text = "".join(t.text or "" for t in child.iter(qn("w:t")))
            fields = [i.text for i in child.iter(qn("w:instrText"))]
            sdt = len(list(child.iter(qn("w:sdt"))))
            print(f"P [{style_id}] {text[:90]!r} fields={fields} sdt={sdt}")
            del para
        elif tag == "tbl":
            rows = child.findall(qn("w:tr"))
            first = ["".join(t.text or "" for t in c.iter(qn("w:t"))) for c in rows[0].findall(qn("w:tc"))]
            print(f"TABLE rows={len(rows)} first_row={first}")
        elif tag == "sdt":
            print("SDT block")
    for section in doc.sections:
        print("HEADER", [p.text for p in section.header.paragraphs if p.text])
        print("FOOTER", [p.text for p in section.footer.paragraphs if p.text])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else str(Path("Templates").glob("QUO*.docx").__next__()))
EOF

export UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv.mac && D=components/alloq-offer/src/alloq_offer/workshop && mkdir -p $D/templates/quo_v1 $D/content $D/export && touch $D/__init__.py $D/content/__init__.py $D/export/__init__.py && cat > scripts/build_quo_layout.py <<'EOF'
"""Build workshop/templates/quo_v1/layout.docx from the QUO customer template.

Keeps the cover and the static legal tail, removes the generated chapters and
replaces customer data by docxtpl placeholders. Run from the repository root.
"""

import copy
import glob
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from docx import Document
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.oxml.ns import qn

TARGET = Path(
    "components/alloq-offer/src/alloq_offer/workshop/templates/quo_v1/layout.docx"
)
ANCHOR = "[[KAPITEL]]"
FIRST_GENERATED = "Management Summary"
FIRST_STATIC_TAIL = "Rechtliche Bestimmungen"

COVER_PLACEHOLDERS = {
    "MVP Referenzdatenbank": "{{ project_title }}",
    "TREYSTA Ingenieure Holding GmbH": "{{ customer_name }}",
    "Kurfürstendamm 29": "{{ customer_street }}",
    "10719 Berlin": "{{ customer_city }}",
    "- Im Folgenden „Treysta” oder „Auftraggeber“ genannt -": (
        "- Im Folgenden „{{ customer_short }}“ oder „Auftraggeber“ genannt -"
    ),
    "Leipzig, 19. Oktober 2026": "Leipzig, {{ offer_date }}",
    "Quote ID: QUO-33441-N7R0Z4": "Quote ID: {{ quote_id }}",
    "Der Auftragnehmer hält sich bis einschließlich zum 30.November.2026 an dieses Angebot gebunden.": (
        "Der Auftragnehmer hält sich bis einschließlich zum {{ validity_date }} an dieses Angebot gebunden."
    ),
}


def text_of(elem) -> str:
    return "".join(t.text or "" for t in elem.iter(qn("w:t")))


def set_text(paragraph, text: str) -> None:
    runs = paragraph.findall(qn("w:r"))
    first = runs[0]
    for run in runs[1:]:
        paragraph.remove(run)
    for t in first.findall(qn("w:t")):
        first.remove(t)
    node = OxmlElement("w:t")
    node.text = text
    node.set("{http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace}space", "preserve")
    first.append(node)


def heading1_index(kids, title: str) -> int:
    for i, kid in enumerate(kids):
        style = kid.find(qn("w:pPr") + "/" + qn("w:pStyle"))
        if (
            kid.tag == qn("w:p")
            and style is not None
            and style.get(qn("w:val")) == "berschrift1"
            and text_of(kid).strip() == title
        ):
            return i
    raise SystemExit(f"heading not found: {title}")


def toc_paragraph(doc: Document):
    title = doc.element.makeelement(qn("w:p"), {})
    ppr = OxmlElement("w:pPr")
    style = OxmlElement("w:pStyle")
    style.set(qn("w:val"), "berschriftohneNummerierung")
    ppr.append(style)
    title.append(ppr)
    run = OxmlElement("w:r")
    t = OxmlElement("w:t")
    t.text = "Inhaltsverzeichnis"
    run.append(t)
    title.append(run)

    para = OxmlElement("w:p")
    for kind, payload in (
        ("begin", None),
        ("instr", ' TOC \\o "1-3" \\h \\z \\u '),
        ("separate", None),
        ("text", "Inhaltsverzeichnis wird beim Öffnen in Word aktualisiert."),
        ("end", None),
    ):
        r = OxmlElement("w:r")
        if kind == "instr":
            node = OxmlElement("w:instrText")
            node.text = payload
            node.set("{http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace}space", "preserve")
        elif kind == "text":
            node = OxmlElement("w:t")
            node.text = payload
        else:
            node = OxmlElement("w:fldChar")
            node.set(qn("w:fldCharType"), kind)
        r.append(node)
        para.append(r)
    return title, para


def main() -> None:
    source = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else glob.glob("Templates/QUO*.docx")[0]
    doc = Document(source)
    body = doc.element.body
    kids = list(body.iterchildren())
    start = heading1_index(kids, FIRST_GENERATED)
    end = heading1_index(kids, FIRST_STATIC_TAIL)
    for kid in kids[start:end]:
        body.remove(kid)

    anchor = copy.deepcopy(kids[start - 2])
    for child in list(anchor):
        anchor.remove(child)
    run = OxmlElement("w:r")
    node = OxmlElement("w:t")
    node.text = ANCHOR
    run.append(node)
    anchor.append(run)
    toc_title, toc = toc_paragraph(doc)
    tail_first = kids[end]
    for elem in (toc_title, toc, anchor):
        tail_first.addprevious(elem)

    for paragraph in body.iter(qn("w:p")):
        replacement = COVER_PLACEHOLDERS.get(text_of(paragraph).strip())
        if replacement is not None:
            set_text(paragraph, replacement)
    for table in body.iter(qn("w:tbl")):
        for paragraph in table.iter(qn("w:p")):
            if text_of(paragraph).strip() == "TREYSTA Ingenieure Holding GmbH":
                set_text(paragraph, "{{ customer_name }}")

    TARGET.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    doc.save(TARGET)
    print(f"written {TARGET}")  # noqa: T201


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Typed chapter content model of the offer workshop.

A chapter holds one of four content types. ``prose`` is the canonical block
tree, ``table`` a plain grid, ``stories`` only settings (the text is resolved
from the story map when rendering) and ``calc`` bound commercial values.
Anything outside this model is rejected with a German message.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from typing import Annotated, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, ValidationError, field_validator

STORY_SCOPES: tuple[str, ...] = ("offen", "angeboten", "option", "ausgeschlossen")
GROUP_BY_VALUES: tuple[str, ...] = ("activity", "slice")

BOUND_FIELDS: dict[str, str] = {
    "offer.person_days": "Personentage",
    "offer.risk_buffer_days": "Risikopuffer (Personentage)",
    "offer.production_cost": "Herstellkosten",
    "offer.recommended_price": "Empfohlener Preis",
    "workspace.currency": "Währung",
    "workspace.validity_date": "Bindefrist",
}


class ContentValidationError(ValueError):
    """Chapter content violates the content model; messages are German."""

    def __init__(self, messages: list[str]) -> None:
        super().__init__("; ".join(messages))
        self.messages = messages


def _new_block_id() -> str:
    return uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]


class Run(BaseModel):
    text: str
    bold: bool = False
    italic: bool = False


Inline = list[Run]


class _Block(BaseModel):
    block_id: str = Field(default_factory=_new_block_id)


class Paragraph(_Block):
    type: Literal["paragraph"] = "paragraph"
    runs: Inline = Field(default_factory=list)


class Heading(_Block):
    type: Literal["heading"] = "heading"
    level: Literal[3, 4] = 3
    runs: Inline = Field(default_factory=list)


class BulletList(_Block):
    type: Literal["bullet_list"] = "bullet_list"
    items: list[Inline] = Field(default_factory=list)


class OrderedList(_Block):
    type: Literal["ordered_list"] = "ordered_list"
    items: list[Inline] = Field(default_factory=list)


class TableBlock(_Block):
    type: Literal["table"] = "table"
    header: list[Inline] = Field(default_factory=list)
    rows: list[list[Inline]] = Field(default_factory=list)

    @field_validator("rows")
    @classmethod
    def _rows_match_header(
        cls, rows: list[list[Inline]], info: object
    ) -> list[list[Inline]]:
        header = getattr(info, "data", {}).get("header", [])
        if any(len(row) != len(header) for row in rows):
            raise ValueError("Jede Tabellenzeile braucht genau so viele Zellen wie die Kopfzeile.")
        return rows


class BoundValue(_Block):
    type: Literal["bound_value"] = "bound_value"
    field: str

    @field_validator("field")
    @classmethod
    def _known_field(cls, value: str) -> str:
        if value not in BOUND_FIELDS:
            raise ValueError(f"Unbekannter Kalkulationswert: {value}")
        return value


ProseBlock = Annotated[
    Paragraph | Heading | BulletList | OrderedList | TableBlock | BoundValue,
    Field(discriminator="type"),
]


class ProseContent(BaseModel):
    chapter_type: Literal["prose"] = "prose"
    blocks: list[ProseBlock] = Field(default_factory=list)


class TableContent(BaseModel):
    chapter_type: Literal["table"] = "table"
    columns: list[str] = Field(min_length=1)
    rows: list[list[Inline]] = Field(default_factory=list)

    @field_validator("rows")
    @classmethod
    def _rows_match_columns(
        cls, rows: list[list[Inline]], info: object
    ) -> list[list[Inline]]:
        columns = getattr(info, "data", {}).get("columns", [])
        if any(len(row) != len(columns) for row in rows):
            raise ValueError("Jede Tabellenzeile braucht genau so viele Zellen wie Spalten.")
        return rows


class StoriesContent(BaseModel):
    """Settings only; stories are resolved from the map revision at render time."""

    chapter_type: Literal["stories"] = "stories"
    scopes: list[str] = Field(default_factory=lambda: ["angeboten", "option"])
    group_by: Literal["activity", "slice"] = "activity"

    @field_validator("scopes")
    @classmethod
    def _known_scopes(cls, scopes: list[str]) -> list[str]:
        unknown = [scope for scope in scopes if scope not in STORY_SCOPES]
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(f"Unbekannter Umfang: {', '.join(unknown)}")
        return scopes


class CalcRow(BaseModel):
    label: str
    field: str

    @field_validator("field")
    @classmethod
    def _known_field(cls, value: str) -> str:
        if value not in BOUND_FIELDS:
            raise ValueError(f"Unbekannter Kalkulationswert: {value}")
        return value


class CalcContent(BaseModel):
    chapter_type: Literal["calc"] = "calc"
    intro: Inline = Field(default_factory=list)
    rows: list[CalcRow] = Field(default_factory=list)


ChapterContent = Annotated[
    ProseContent | TableContent | StoriesContent | CalcContent,
    Field(discriminator="chapter_type"),
]

CHAPTER_TYPES: tuple[str, ...] = ("prose", "table", "stories", "calc")


def plain_text(runs: Inline) -> str:
    return "".join(run.text for run in runs)


def parse_content(data: dict) -> ProseContent | TableContent | StoriesContent | CalcContent:
    """Validate raw JSON content; raise ``ContentValidationError`` in German."""
    from pydantic import TypeAdapter

    chapter_type = data.get("chapter_type") if isinstance(data, dict) else None
    if chapter_type not in CHAPTER_TYPES:
        raise ContentValidationError(["Unbekannter Kapiteltyp."])
    try:
        return TypeAdapter(ChapterContent).validate_python(data)
    except ValidationError as exc:
        messages = [_german(err) for err in exc.errors()]
        raise ContentValidationError(messages) from exc


def _german(error: dict) -> str:
    message = str(error.get("msg", ""))
    if message.startswith("Value error, "):
        return message.removeprefix("Value error, ")
    location = ".".join(str(part) for part in error.get("loc", ()))
    if error.get("type") == "union_tag_invalid":
        return f"Nicht unterstützter Inhaltsbaustein ({location})."
    return f"Ungültiger Inhalt ({location})."
EOF

"""Template package: chapter catalogue, rules and Word layout of one template."""

from __future__ import annotations

import io
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Literal

import yaml
from docx import Document
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, model_validator

from alloq_offer.workshop.content.schema import CHAPTER_TYPES

TEMPLATES_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "templates"
DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_KEY = "quo_v1"
CHAPTER_ANCHOR = "[[KAPITEL]]"


class TemplateError(ValueError):
    """The template package is inconsistent."""


class ChapterDef(BaseModel):
    key: str
    title: str
    level: Literal[1, 2] = 1
    required: bool = False
    chapter_type: Literal["prose", "table", "stories", "calc"]
    defaults: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    guiding_question: str = ""
    content_rules: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)


class TemplatePackage(BaseModel):
    key: str
    version: str
    chapters: list[ChapterDef]
    static_chapters: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    rules: dict[str, dict[str, list[str]]] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    layout_path: Path

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _unique_keys(self) -> TemplatePackage:
        keys = [chapter.key for chapter in self.chapters]
        if len(keys) != len(set(keys)):
            raise TemplateError("Kapitelschlüssel müssen eindeutig sein.")
        if any(chapter.chapter_type not in CHAPTER_TYPES for chapter in self.chapters):
            raise TemplateError("Unbekannter Kapiteltyp in der Vorlage.")
        return self

    def chapter(self, key: str) -> ChapterDef:
        for chapter in self.chapters:
            if chapter.key == key:
                return chapter
        raise KeyError(key)

    def layout_bytes(self) -> bytes:
        return self.layout_path.read_bytes()

    def check_layout(self) -> None:
        """Fail unless the layout holds the chapter anchor exactly once."""
        document = Document(io.BytesIO(self.layout_bytes()))
        anchors = [p for p in document.paragraphs if p.text.strip() == CHAPTER_ANCHOR]
        if len(anchors) != 1:
            raise TemplateError(
                f"Die Vorlage braucht genau einen Anker {CHAPTER_ANCHOR}."
            )


def load_template(
    key: str = DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_KEY, root: Path = TEMPLATES_ROOT
) -> TemplatePackage:
    base = root / key
    chapters_doc = yaml.safe_load((base / "chapters.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    rules_doc = yaml.safe_load((base / "rules.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    package = TemplatePackage(
        key=key,
        version=chapters_doc["version"],
        chapters=[ChapterDef(**item) for item in chapters_doc["chapters"]],
        static_chapters=chapters_doc.get("static_chapters", []),
        rules=rules_doc.get("chapters", {}),
        layout_path=base / "layout.docx",
    )
    package.check_layout()
    return package
